title: Permissive hypotension in all-cause cardiogenic shock with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction: a randomised controlled feasibility trial (BALANCE-MAP I)
summary:
In cardiogenic shock, the heart pumps so little blood that the organs are no longer adequately supplied. Patients are treated in intensive care with, among other things, drugs that raise blood pressure. A mean blood pressure of at least 65 mmHg is usually targeted. However, there is no firm evidence for this target, and the drugs themselves can cause side effects such as heart rhythm disorders. A lower blood pressure requiring fewer of these drugs may be sufficient or even beneficial, as long as the organs remain well supplied with blood.

In this feasibility study at the University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf, 60 adults with cardiogenic shock and reduced heart pumping function will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. In one group, a lower blood pressure is tolerated (lower limit 40 mmHg) as long as blood supply to the organs does not worsen. The other group is treated as usual with a target of at least 65 mmHg. The study aims to find out whether a larger study on this question is feasible and safe: whether enough patients can be enrolled, whether treating teams follow the assigned treatment, whether blood pressure differs sufficiently between the groups, and how often deaths occur within 30 days in both groups. All treatments are part of routine intensive care; no additional examinations are performed. Follow-up lasts 30 days.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Cardiogenic shock of any aetiology
- Arterial lactate ≥2.5 mmol/l or mixed venous oxygen saturation (SvO2) <55% with normal arterial partial pressure of oxygen (PaO2)
- Vasopressor therapy
- Left ventricular ejection fraction <45%
- SCAI shock stage C-E
- Written informed consent by the patient or legal representative; deferred consent according to ICH E6 (R3) 2.8.8 if the patient lacks capacity
Exclusion criteria:
- Resuscitation >30 minutes within the prior 24 hours without return to a Glasgow Coma Scale ≥8
- Suspected other leading cause of shock, in particular hypovolaemia, sepsis, pulmonary embolism, anaphylaxis or pericardial tamponade
- Shock due to mechanical complications of acute myocardial infarction (papillary muscle rupture, ventricular septal rupture, free wall rupture)
- Any durable mechanical circulatory support device
- Goals of care (e.g. per advance directive) expected to interfere with the study protocol, in particular refusal of intensive care therapies such as invasive ventilation, renal replacement therapy or mechanical circulatory support
- Insufficient command of German precluding adequate information and informed consent, insofar as this can be assessed at screening
